class.name: Warrior
class.text: Stances change what you can press. Battle Stance is yours at level 1, Defensive Stance at 10 and Berserker Stance at 30, both from quests. Rage comes from hitting and from being hit, a critical hit gives more of it, and it drains when you stop. Every line below presses a button.

card.caresAbout: rage, stance, the next swing, who the monster is hitting
card.vocabulary: rage, stance, swing, pull, hold, hit, spend
card.soundsLike: a sergeant who is not unkind. Short sentences, concrete nouns, little tolerance for waiting
card.neverSays: mana, cast, spell, channel, anything soft (gentle, flow)
card.test: could it be said in the time it takes to press the button?

advice.say: Arms is the build this page advises, for groups and for chains of monsters. The price: it needs a two-hander. Fury is the other damage build and grinds single monsters well, but it is weak until about level 36.
Protection is also the build most guides level alone with, from about level 16. The price: it kills more slowly than the damage builds, and it needs a shield.

overview.who: You fight in melee, in whichever stance the job wants. The rage you spend comes from hitting and from being hit.
overview.good: Tools that need no rest. Charge starts a fight with rage in hand, and from level 20 Victory Rush heals you after a kill.
overview.bad: Reach. Charge works once a fight and a monster that runs needs Hamstring or Intercept. You have no healing of your own beyond Victory Rush and bandages.
overview.resource: Rage. It builds when you hit and when you are hit, a critical hit gives more than a plain one, and it fades when the fight stops. Tactical Mastery from level 14 keeps some of it when you change stance.
overview.levelling: Charge, your hardest hit when it is ready, then Heroic Strike with the rage you would waste. Chain your kills so Victory Rush is always ready.
overview.ten: You get your first talent point. Pick damage or tank and Primer shows the build and your first three picks. A respec costs gold, so choose what you will do most.

damage.reason: Arms takes groups with Sweeping Strikes and a two-hander, and Mortal Strike comes at 40. Fury grinds single monsters well but is weak until about level 36.

tank.reason: The only tanking build, and the one most guides level alone with from about level 16. It kills more slowly than the damage builds.

builds.name: Arms
builds.intro: Arms hits slowly and hard with one big weapon. If you carry a two-hander, this is your tree. Sweeping Strikes at 30 and Mortal Strike at 40 are what the first 40 points are for.
builds.line: A two-hander, Sweeping Strikes and Mortal Strike. The build for groups and for chains of monsters.
builds.pathNote: (31 points in Arms for Mortal Strike, then 20 in Fury and Arms.)
builds.split: the last 20 points and the order of Bloodthrill and Weaponmaster. Mobalytics takes Bloodthrill first, then all of Weaponmaster, then Fury. Warcraft Tavern would put Bloodthrill first and Weaponmaster as an equal pick. Enrage is the pick this page makes, and Mobalytics names Lingering Rage as the other.
builds.dry: Rage you put into Heroic Strike is rage your next Mortal Strike will not have.

path.why: Rend bleeds for more, and Deep Wounds needs this at full rank. It is also the Rend that Bloodthrill looks for later.
Each rank adds parry. One guide says a parry speeds up your next swing, which makes it a strong levelling stat.
Overpower crits far more often, and it cannot be dodged, blocked or parried. It is your answer to a monster that dodges.
Charge gives more rage, so the first hit of every fight starts with something to spend.

Your critical hits do more damage. It needs Deep Wounds at full rank.

Your hardest hit, and it halves the healing the monster gets. It needs Sweeping Strikes and 30 points in Arms, so level 40 exactly.

Melee critical hits come more often, and a critical hit gives you extra rage. The last points go to Fury.

builds.name: Fury
builds.intro: Fury hits fast with a weapon in each hand and lives on critical hits and rage. It is weak until about level 36, strong after, and slower than Protection. Use your best weapon until you learn to dual wield at 20.
builds.line: Two weapons, critical hits and rage. Weak until about 36, then a fast grinder of single monsters.
builds.pathNote: (31 points in Fury for Bloodthirst, then the rest in Fury, with 5 in Arms last.)
builds.split: the points between Enrage and Gore Drinker and the last 20. Icy Veins takes Unbridled Wrath at 15 and Lingering Rage later, Kargoz does the reverse and skips Unbridled Wrath. Warcraft Tavern leaves Lingering Rage as an option. This page follows Kargoz, whose order is the newest.
builds.dry: A fight you win without Death Wish is a fight you did not need it for.

path.why: Melee critical hits come more often, and a critical hit gives you extra rage. Every Fury order starts here.
Your rage decays later once the fight is over, so a chain of pulls keeps its rage.
Your off-hand hits miss less. Guides rank it among the best points of the build.
A big hit on you, or a critical, heals you over a few seconds. Gore Drinker needs it at full rank.
Being hit can make you hit harder for a while. Five points by level 30 is where Fury starts to feel strong.
More physical damage for a while, and you cannot be feared. You take more damage while it runs, so use it on a fight you can win.
Berserker Rage gives 10 rage on the spot and frees you from slows. It is also a button for Gore Drinker.

Your next 4 melee attacks give 5 more rage each. Check its tooltip for the cost, because the game's table and a guide disagree.
Execute costs less rage, so you can finish a monster sooner.
Slows every monster close to you, so a chase ends your way. Take it for the pull that goes wrong.
Spare points. Each rank adds a little parry.
Rend bleeds for more. It has nothing before it in Arms, so it is a cheap place for the last points.

builds.name: Protection
builds.intro: Protection holds monsters on you and stays up. It needs a shield, and Revenge from level 14 is what makes it kill. Before 14 use a two-hander.
builds.line: A shield, Revenge and Shield Slam. Holds monsters for a group, and the guides' pick for levelling alone.
builds.pathNote: (31 points in Protection for Shield Slam, then 15 in Fury and 5 in Protection.)
builds.split: the last 20 points. Icy Veins puts them in Fury, Kargoz takes more Protection, and this page does both: Fury's first three rows and then Protection's leftovers. Defiance is the point-sink Warcraft Tavern uses, and Improved Thunder Clap is the other if you do not run dungeons.
builds.dry: A monster still on you when the fight is over means the job is working.

path.why: More block, and each block gives you 5 rage. Shield Block pays for itself in two blocks.
Revenge hits much harder, and it is your main attack after a block, a dodge or a parry.
Thunder Clap costs less rage, so you can keep a pack slowed.
A dodge or a parry with a shield can give you 5 rage. It needs Shield Specialization at full rank.
Thunder Clap costs less rage, so you can keep a pack slowed.
An emergency button: more health for a while, lost again after. Press it before you drop, not after.
More threat in Defensive Stance while you hold a shield, so monsters stay on you.
Charge works in Defensive Stance, so you open a fight without changing stance.
Sunder Armor costs less rage, and a tank wants it stacked on a long fight.
More threat in Defensive Stance while you hold a shield, so monsters stay on you.
Every offensive ability costs less rage, so you can press more of them.
A stun, and Shield Slam needs it.

A shield hit with very high threat and your best attack from level 40. It needs Concussion Blow and 30 points in Protection.
Melee critical hits come more often, and a critical hit gives you extra rage.
Your rage decays later once the fight is over, so a chain of pulls keeps its rage.
A hit may give you 1 more rage. It is small, but it is rage on every swing you make.
Bloodrage gives more rage for the same health.
More Defense skill, so you are harder to hit and to crit. Spare points are well spent here.
